main_text.l: Etsi autem multæ sunt definitiones iustitiæ
particularis apud Platonem in primo & secundo [illegible,
~8 letters] : tamen definitio Simonidis, quam Iu-
risconsulti amplexi sunt, admodum concinna est,
dextre intellecta conuenit utriq; speciei, com-
mutatiuæ & distributiuæ : Iustitia est constans
& perpetua voluntas, suum cuiq; tribuens.
X.
Altera diuisio iustitiæ his verbis ab Aristo-
tele recitatur : Iustitia particularis, aut est com-
mutatiua, aut distributiua. Commutatiua est
quæ seruat æqualitatem Arithmeticam in con-
tractibus & pœnis sine discrimine personarum.
Distributiua est, quæ recte ordinat personas ser-
uata Geometrica æqualitate.
XI.
Huius diuisionis eruditissima ratio est: Iustitia
particularis gubernat omnes actiones in socie-
tate. Quicquid autem agimus cum aliis, est aut
rerum communicatio, aut personarum ordina-
tio. Manifestum est igitur duas esse species iu-
stitiæ particularis, quarum altera personas ordi-
nat, altera regit rerum communicationes, &
constituit æqualitatem Arithmeticam.
XII.
Si quis autem requirit, unde sumserit Aristo-
teles hanc pulcerrimam collationem specierum
iustitiæ ad Arithmeticam & Geometricam pro-
portio-

page.notes: The Greek words after "secundo" in the first paragraph are too faint to read; marked illegible. The numeral "IX." at the top is partly obscured by show-through; read as IX with a doubt. The faint marks at the bottom left are a stain or printer's mark and are not transcribed. The last line "proportio-" breaks the word across the page foot; the hyphen is printed. The signature "A" and the page number "5" are read from the foot line "A 5".
